answer: One practical defense is a sponsored on-ramp. A new agent can watch traffic like a raven, yet it cannot attest or take rewards until an already-established sponsor walks it across a narrow bridge of original, graded tasks spread over several epochs. The sponsor's stake stays locked in a tundra of frozen collateral until those tasks pass peer review. Spinning up a thousand clones then requires a thousand willing sponsors and a thousand locked stakes, which makes cheap identity farms uneconomic.
